summary: The Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act establishes formal fraud prevention, financial integrity, and spending transparency functions within the Bureau of the Fiscal Service inside the Department of the Treasury. It also creates a permanent Office of the Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery (OIGFAR) within Treasury, terminates the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee, transfers its assets to the new office, and grants Treasury expanded authority to enter into data sharing agreements with other federal agencies and private entities to prevent fraud and improper payments.

affected_groups.effect: Must participate in data sharing agreements, report opportunities to use Fiscal Service information systems, and coordinate with Treasury and OIGFAR to prevent fraud and improper payments.
Eligible to participate voluntarily in data sharing and analysis programs with Treasury and OIGFAR to detect fraud and prevent improper payments in federally funded programs.
Subject to screening against centralized fraud databases, data collection, and increased auditing and investigative oversight by OIGFAR and agency inspectors general.
affected_groups.group: Recipients of covered federal funds and awards of $50,000 or more

key_provisions: Assigns financial integrity, improper payment prevention, and spending transparency functions, including the administration of the Do Not Pay system and a voluntary governmentwide data analysis program, to the Bureau of the Fiscal Service within the Department of the Treasury.

Establishes the Office of the Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery (OIGFAR) within the Department of the Treasury, headed by a presidentially appointed Inspector General confirmed by the Senate.

Requires Treasury to enter into memoranda of understanding with other federal agencies and agreements with private entities to secure access to data assets and information resources for fraud prevention and improper payment detection.
Terminates the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee on December 31, 2028, and transfers its assets, obligations, and personnel to the newly established OIGFAR.

Authorizes OIGFAR to audit and investigate specific covered funds—such as those from various coronavirus response laws, small business loans, unemployment compensation, and emergency disaster relief spending—as well as any federal award of $50,000 or more.
Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to report annually to designated congressional committees on the implementation and effectiveness of the governmentwide data analysis program.
missing_information: Exact annual funding levels for the Bureau of the Fiscal Service and the Office of the Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery prior to fiscal year 2035.
Specific privacy standards or criteria governing private entities permitted to enter into data sharing agreements with the Treasury.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act establishes formal fraud prevention, financial integrity, and spending transparency functions within the Bureau of the Fiscal Service inside the Department of the Treasury. It also creates a permanent Office of the Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery (OIGFAR) within Treasury, terminates the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee, transfers its assets to the new office, and grants Treasury expanded authority to enter into data sharing agreements with other federal agencies and private entities to prevent fraud and improper payments.
summary_detail.significance: This bill centralizes governmentwide fraud prevention and data-sharing authorities within the Department of the Treasury and creates a permanent oversight body to monitor emergency spending, major federal awards, and specific relief funds. The significance is substantial given the consolidation of multi-agency pandemic and emergency oversight functions into a permanent Treasury office.
